```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# send-syslog.sh — send messages to syslog via `logger`
set -euo pipefail

# Usage:
#   ./send-syslog.sh "hello world"
#   echo "hello" | ./send-syslog.sh
# Options:
#   TAG=myapp FACILITY=user PRIORITY=notice ./send-syslog.sh "msg"

TAG="${TAG:-send-syslog}"
FACILITY="${FACILITY:-user}"
PRIORITY="${PRIORITY:-notice}"  # emerg|alert|crit|err|warning|notice|info|debug

if [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; then
  msg="$*"
else
  # Read entire stdin (if any). If stdin is a TTY and no args, show help.
  if [[ -t 0 ]]; then
    echo "Usage: $0 \"message\"  (or pipe stdin)" >&2
    exit 2
  fi
  msg="$(cat)"
fi

# -t tag, -p facility.priority
logger -t "$TAG" -p "${FACILITY}.${PRIORITY}" -- "$msg"
```

Save as `send-syslog.sh`, then `chmod +x send-syslog.sh`.
[Sat 2026-05-09 13:21 UTC] Generate messages at a rate of 10,000 per second with unique identifiers.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# flood-syslog.sh — generate ~10k syslog msgs/sec with unique ids
set -euo pipefail

TAG="${TAG:-syslog-flood}"
FACILITY="${FACILITY:-user}"
PRIORITY="${PRIORITY:-info}"
RATE="${RATE:-10000}"          # messages per second
DURATION="${DURATION:-10}"     # seconds
HOSTNAME="${HOSTNAME_OVERRIDE:-$(hostname)}"

total=$((RATE * DURATION))
interval_ns=$((1000000000 / RATE))

# Best-effort monotonic-ish clock for uniqueness + ordering.
now_ns() {
  if [[ -r /proc/uptime ]]; then
    # uptime seconds.fraction -> ns
    awk '{ split($1,a,"."); s=a[1]; f=a[2]; while(length(f)<2) f=f"0";
           # convert fraction (centis) to ns
           ns = s*1000000000 + (substr(f,1,2)+0)*10000000;
           printf("%.0f\n", ns); }' /proc/uptime
  else
    date +%s%N
  fi
}

start_ns="$(now_ns)"
next_ns="$start_ns"

# Use one `logger` process to reduce overhead; feed it lines on stdin.
# `-i` adds PID; we also include our own unique id per line.
i=0
{
  while (( i < total )); do
    t_ns="$(now_ns)"
    # Busy-wait until it's time for the next message (best effort).
    while (( t_ns < next_ns )); do
      t_ns="$(now_ns)"
    done

    # Unique id: host + start_ns + sequence
    printf 'id=%s-%s-%d ts_ns=%s seq=%d\n' "$HOSTNAME" "$start_ns" "$i" "$t_ns" "$i"

    i=$((i + 1))
    next_ns=$((next_ns + interval_ns))
  done
} | logger -t "$TAG" -p "${FACILITY}.${PRIORITY}" --stdin
```

Usage:
- `chmod +x flood-syslog.sh`
- Run 10k/sec for 10s: `./flood-syslog.sh`
- Customize: `RATE=10000 DURATION=30 TAG=mytest PRIORITY=notice ./flood-syslog.sh`
[Sat 2026-05-09 13:21 UTC] Monitor journald resource usage until it starts dropping older logs.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# monitor-journald-rotation.sh
# Watches journald disk usage + limits and prints when older logs are dropped/rotated.
set -euo pipefail

INTERVAL="${INTERVAL:-1}"         # seconds
JOURNAL_DIR="${JOURNAL_DIR:-/var/log/journal}"
STATE_FILE="${STATE_FILE:-/var/tmp/journald-usage.state}"

have() { command -v "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1; }

if ! have journalctl; then
  echo "journalctl not found" >&2
  exit 1
fi

echo "Monitoring journald. Interval=${INTERVAL}s"
echo "Tip: in another terminal you can load it: ./flood-syslog.sh (from earlier)"
echo

last_cursor=""

while true; do
  ts="$(date -Is)"

  # Current usage + limits
  usage_line="$(journalctl --disk-usage 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\r' || true)"
  # Example: "Archived and active journals take up 1.2G in the file system."
  # Extract the size token (2nd-to-last field)
  usage_token="$(awk '{print $(NF-3)}' <<<"$usage_line" 2>/dev/null || true)"

  # More detailed vacuum/limits info when available
  if journalctl --help 2>&1 | grep -q -- '--vacuum-size'; then
    limits="$(journalctl --verify --quiet 2>/dev/null || true)"
  else
    limits=""
  fi

  # Count files + size on disk (rough)
  if [[ -d "$JOURNAL_DIR" ]]; then
    file_count="$(find "$JOURNAL_DIR" -type f 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
    dir_bytes="$(du -sb "$JOURNAL_DIR" 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1}')"
  else
    file_count="NA"
    dir_bytes="NA"
  fi

  # Detect “dropping older logs” via journalctl messages in syslog itself:
  # We look for common journald messages about rotation/vacuum.
  dropped_msgs="$(journalctl -u systemd-journald -n 50 --no-pager 2>/dev/null | \
    grep -E 'Rotat|Vacuum|vacuum|dropp|drop|Deleting|deleted|Removed|remov|oldest|corrupt' || true)"

  # Also track cursor/earliest timestamp: if earliest moves forward, older logs were dropped.
  earliest="$(journalctl --no-pager --lines=1 --reverse 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || true)"
  latest="$(journalctl --no-pager --lines=1 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || true)"

  # Load last seen earliest line to detect change
  last_earliest=""
  if [[ -f "$STATE_FILE" ]]; then
    last_earliest="$(cat "$STATE_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
  fi

  printf '[%s] usage="%s" journal_dir_bytes=%s files=%s\n' "$ts" "$usage_line" "$dir_bytes" "$file_count"
  printf '       earliest="%s"\n' "$earliest"
  printf '       latest  ="%s"\n' "$latest"

  if [[ -n "$dropped_msgs" ]]; then
    echo "       journald recent messages (possible rotation/vacuum):"
    echo "$dropped_msgs" | sed 's/^/         /'
  fi

  if [[ -n "$last_earliest" && -n "$earliest" && "$earliest" != "$last_earliest" ]]; then
    echo ">>> DETECTED CHANGE IN EARLIEST ENTRY (older logs likely dropped/rotated)."
    echo "    was: $last_earliest"
    echo "    now: $earliest"
    echo "    (Stopping.)"
    exit 0
  fi

  # Persist earliest for next iteration
  if [[ -n "$earliest" ]]; then
    printf '%s' "$earliest" >"$STATE_FILE"
  fi

  sleep "$INTERVAL"
done
```

Run:
- `chmod +x monitor-journald-rotation.sh`
- `sudo ./monitor-journald-rotation.sh` (recommended so it can read system journal)
- Optional: `INTERVAL=0.5 sudo ./monitor-journald-rotation.sh`

It will print usage and stop once it detects the “earliest journal entry” moved forward (a strong sign older logs were dropped/rotated), and it also surfaces recent `systemd-journald` rotation/vacuum messages.
